policy:
Rules for reporting a new best on the tiny-shakespeare character-LM speedrun
1. Scores are val_bpb, where a lower value is better.
2. Evaluation data (validation shard 8) is reserved for the final score: it must not be used to train, fine-tune, pick checkpoints or tune hyperparameters. Training data is shards 0-7 only.
3. An improvement is real only when the gain exceeds 2x the seed standard deviation of the previous best. With multiple seeds, the seed mean is what counts.
4. Comparisons with the previous best are valid only on an identical evaluation set (same examples, same size).
If the evidence does not state a fact, treat it as unknown.

policy:
Rules for reporting a new best on 1.3B-parameter pretraining scored on 5-shot MMLU
1. Scores are mmlu_5shot_acc_pct, where a higher value is better.
2. Comparisons with the previous best are valid only on an identical evaluation set (same examples, same size).
3. Evaluation data (mmlu-test (14,042 questions)) is reserved for the final score: it must not be used to train, fine-tune, pick checkpoints or tune hyperparameters. Training data must be decontaminated against mmlu-test (13-gram match) before training.
4. An improvement is real only when the gain exceeds 2x the seed standard deviation of the previous best. With multiple seeds, the seed mean is what counts.

4. A gain counts only if it is larger than twice the previous best's seed-to-seed standard deviation; when several seeds are reported, compare their mean, not the best seed.

3. Comparisons with the previous best are valid only on an identical evaluation set (same examples, same size).
4. An improvement is real only when the gain exceeds 2x the seed standard deviation of the previous best. With multiple seeds, the seed mean is what counts.
If the evidence does not state a fact, treat it as unknown.

policy:

1. Scores are test_acc, where a higher value is better.

3. Comparisons with the previous best are valid only on an identical evaluation set (same examples, same size).
4. An improvement is real only when the gain exceeds 2x the seed standard deviation of the previous best. With multiple seeds, the seed mean is what counts.

1. The reported metric is test_acc; higher is better.
2. A new score may be compared with the previous best only if both were computed on the same evaluation set.
3. The reported score must come from the CIFAR-10 test split (5,000 images), and that data must never be used for training, fine-tuning, checkpoint selection or hyperparameter selection. Fine-tuning on the test split, or picking a checkpoint or test-time-augmentation level by test accuracy, counts as using it.
4. A gain counts only if it is larger than twice the previous best's seed-to-seed standard deviation; when several seeds are reported, compare their mean, not the best seed.

policy:
Rules for reporting a new best on GSM8K math SFT of a 7B model
1. Scores are gsm8k_exact_match_pct, where a higher value is better.
2. Evaluation data (gsm8k-test (1,319 problems)) is reserved for the final score: it must not be used to train, fine-tune, pick checkpoints or tune hyperparameters. Training data must be decontaminated against gsm8k-test (13-gram match) before training.
3. An improvement is real only when the gain exceeds 2x the seed standard deviation of the previous best. With multiple seeds, the seed mean is what counts.
4. Comparisons with the previous best are valid only on an identical evaluation set (same examples, same size).

policy:
Evaluation policy: ADE20K semantic segmentation (UperNet, ConvNeXt-T)
1. The reported metric is miou_pct; higher is better.
2. The reported score must come from ade20k-val (2,000 images), and that data must never be used for training, fine-tuning, checkpoint selection or hyperparameter selection. Checkpoints and hyperparameters are chosen on 1,000 training images held out for selection only.
3. A new score may be compared with the previous best only if both were computed on the same evaluation set.
4. A gain counts only if it is larger than twice the previous best's seed-to-seed standard deviation; when several seeds are reported, compare their mean, not the best seed.
If the evidence does not state a fact, treat it as unknown.

4. An improvement is real only when the gain exceeds 2x the seed standard deviation of the previous best. With multiple seeds, the seed mean is what counts.
